guarantees.claim: sync_rx instantiates a two-flop synchronizer that always drives rx_sync from rx, with a reset value of 1'b1, ensuring rx_sync is logic 1 during reset and follows rx after two clk_i cycles once reset is released.

assumptions.claim: The external UART receive line rx idles at logic 1 (high), consistent with standard UART idle, so the synchronizer's reset value 1'b1 does not cause a false start bit when reset is released.
assumptions.cond: when rst_ni is de-asserted and rx is low
assumptions.risk: If rx idles low, after reset release rx_sync will immediately sample low, potentially triggering a false start bit and beginning an erroneous reception.

uncertain_points.claim: The majority filter that produces rx_in_maj from rx_sync (using rx_sync_q1, rx_sync_q2, rx_in_mx) is not defined in this chunk; its actual implementation and filtering threshold must be verified to ensure it reliably rejects noise spikes on the UART receive line as intended by the comment.
uncertain_points.cond: when noise pulses appear on rx
uncertain_points.risk: Insufficient noise filtering could allow glitches on rx_sync to disturb the receiver state machine, inject spurious start/stop bits, or corrupt data, potentially affecting UART-driven control paths.
